jobs.title: AI Engineer
jobs.jd: Welcome to Nutrium Before you apply, here's the key thing: our mission is to promote global well-being by making quality 1:1 nutrition accessible to everyone. A lot has changed since we started, but our mission is still at the heart of everything we do — it's written in our culture book, in our proposals, in our docs, and it guides every decision we make. It’s also what allowed us, for years, to improve the experience of nutrition professionals and their patients through the world's #1 nutrition counseling platform. But we didn't stop there. Today, with Nutrium Care, we're taking the next step: bringing real, personalized nutrition to people anytime, anywhere, and helping them build healthier, happier lives. Along the way, we raised our Series A and surpassed €15M in funding, partnered with global leaders like Vodafone, Adidas, Wellhub, and Linde, and reached millions of people around the world. From day one, we also knew something else: building this future would take more than great tech. It would take a place where talented people can grow, feel supported, and actually enjoy the journey along the way. You go first We're proud of our journey so far, and we believe there's space for more people to shine, challenge us, and help shape what comes next. ⭐ What you will bring You bring experience in AI and applying modern technologies like LLMs to solve real product challenges. You will take technical ownership of AI-driven features, collaborating closely with Product and Engineering in a fast-paced environment to shape solutions from discovery through delivery. You will build and take ownership of AI-powered features/solutions, making thoughtful technical decisions that improve workflows and decision-making for dietitians and patients, with a tangible impact on a platform used by thousands. ⭐ What you will be doing Build and take ownership of AI-powered features designed to enhance Nutrium 's platform. Apply Generative AI technologies, such as LLMs and RAG architectures, to address practical product challenges. Continuously monitor, troubleshoot, and fine-tune AI solutions, ensuring a balance between key performance metrics and business requirements. Establish evaluation strategies and quality metrics (including groundedness, safety, latency, and cost) and work to continuously enhance them. Partner with Product, Engineering, and dietitians to transform requirements into robust, testable AI solutions. Create and maintain thorough documentation, lead technical discussions, and drive knowledge-sharing initiatives to elevate team practices. ⭐ You might be a great fit if you... Have 1-3 years of experience building AI-powered solutions. Hold a degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Data Science, or equivalent practical experience. Build and code hands-on solutions using LLMs in real-world projects. Have specific experience with LLMs, RAG systems, and vector databases. Evaluate and improve AI systems through measurement and iteration. Are comfortable working with a high degree of autonomy, taking ownership of problems, and driving solutions. Are a strong problem-solver who values collaboration, clear communication, and taking initiative. Demonstrate commitment to building with privacy and security in mind, including comfort working with sensitive data. Bonus : Are based in the north of Portugal (Braga/Porto); Are fluent in both Portuguese and English. Now, it's our turn Transparency is one of our core values, so here's exactly what you can expect from Nutrium : Gross annual salary : €25,200 - €39,200, depending on your experience. Perks and benefits: A flexible work model and hours 27 days of annual leave Unlimited nutritional appointments (via Nutrium Care) Unlimited psychology sessions Health insurance Meal allowance: 10,46€ per working day Professional development budget Snacks and good coffee in the offices A multicultural team that enjoys spending time together, not just while working, but also through team activities, social events, and our annual offsite. 🚀 How we'll get to know each other A quick overview of what our hiring journey looks like: CV Screening First interview with the recruiter Technical interview with the hiring manager A take-home challenge, sent by email Final Interview (with challenge discussion) We're committed to making our hiring process fair, inclusive, and human. We aim to build a team that reflects the diversity of the world we live in. That means welcoming people of all races, ethnicities, genders, sexual orientations, ages, abilities, religions, and backgrounds. If you're excited about this role but your experience doesn't align perfectly with every requirement, we still encourage you to apply. You might be exactly who we're looking for. jobs.title: Senior AI Engineer (CCC Casualty / Claims Intelligence)
jobs.jd: CCC Intelligent Solutions Inc. (CCC) is a leading cloud platform for the multi-trillion-dollar insurance economy , creating intelligent experiences for insurers, repairers, automakers, part suppliers, and more. At CCC, we’re making life just work by empowering more than 35,000 businesses with industry-leading technology to get drivers back on the road and to health quickly and seamlessly. We’re pushing boundaries with innovative AI solutions that simplify and enhance the claims and repair journey. Through purposeful innovation and the strength of its connections, CCC technologies empower the people and industry relied upon to keep lives moving forward when it matters most. Learn more about CCC at . The Role As a Senior AI Engineer, you'll own agents end to end within a problem area, from the first prototype to measured performance in production. You'll join a new engineering group at CCC building AI-native products for our auto casualty business, the injury side of auto claims. The group is small and senior, and it's growing fast. Our teams work on: Medical bills: AI products that help claims teams handle the medical bills on injury claims accurately and efficiently. Claims decision support: products that help claims professionals make better, faster decisions on injury claims. Agentic Rules Platform: the rules engine and agentic tooling behind decisions across our casualty products, plus the evaluation infrastructure every team relies on. You'll build the AI agents behind our products. They work with complex documents and claim data, call tools, and support claims experts in their daily work. You'll own the orchestration, retrieval, evaluations, and guardrails that make them safe to rely on, and you'll write the production code to ship them. Salary range is: $180,000 - 225,000 This position is bonus eligible. Key Responsibilities: Design and build LLM-powered agents and workflows: orchestration, tool use, retrieval, structured extraction, and human-in-the-loop review Build evaluations with data labelers and subject matter experts, and run them on every change Make agents production-grade: guardrails, observability, cost and latency, and careful handling of sensitive health data What success looks like: In your first month, you've shipped a measured improvement to an existing agent. By six months, an agent you built is in production with customers, backed by evaluation results. Requirements: Typically 5+ years of professional software or ML engineering experience, including meaningful recent work with LLMs Strong production engineering skills in Python, including API services, and comfort working in TypeScript At least a year of shipping LLM-powered products to real users, including retrieval (RAG, embeddings, vector search) and prompt engineering Experience designing evaluations for non-deterministic systems, and the habit of measuring before and after every change A quantitative mindset: you're comfortable with metrics, sampling, error analysis, and knowing when a result is real Real experience shipping faster with AI-assisted or agentic engineering tools, with examples you can walk us through Nice to have: Document understanding, OCR, or extraction from complex documents Experience fine-tuning LLMs or working with multimodal data Interview Policy & Privacy Notice: A video interview is required for this position. Video interviews are transcribed. Transcriptions are retained and may be reviewed by CCC and our recruiters. Candidates are not permitted to use generative AI or automated assistance during the interviews unless explicitly allowed by the interview team for a specific exercise. Our Job Applicant Privacy Notice is available HERE. About CCC's Commitment to Employees: CCC Intelligent Solutions understands that our employees play an integral role in our vision to shape a world where life just works. Our team is defined by our values of Integrity, Customer-Focus, Innovation, Inclusion & Diversity, Tenacity, and Connection. Through diverse perspectives, purposeful innovation, and the strength of connections, our technologies empower the people and industry relied upon to keep lives moving forward when it matters most. At CCC, together everyone can thrive as we innovate and collaborate, creating employee experiences that just work. We are committed to providing opportunities for our people to make real-life impacts, advance in their careers, and contribute to CCC’s success. CCC offers competitive compensation and benefits to support you and your families, including: 401K Match Paid time off Annual Incentive Plan Performance Bonus Comprehensive health insurance Adoption Assistance Tuition Reimbursement Wellness Programs Stock Purchase Plan options Employee Resource Groups For more information about our benefits, please check out our careers site. Here, you belong. You are seen, valued, and respected. We celebrate you for who you are and all you bring. Every voice is heard and is important to our success. jobs.title: Data Engineer II, Alexa AI - ML Engineering
jobs.jd: Join Alexa AI - ML Engineering and help power personalized, proactive experiences for hundreds of millions of Alexa customers worldwide. As a Data Engineer II, you will design and own the large-scale data pipelines that turn raw customer-interaction signals into the context and features our personalization and proactive-agent models depend on, working side-by-side with SDEs to shape our data strategy and architecture. - You will build and operate ETL/ELT pipelines processing billions of records a day, using AWS big-data services (Glue, EMR, Kinesis, Redshift, DynamoDB) and distributed compute. - You will partner with SDEs and applied scientists to define data strategy, contracts, and feature pipelines, and to decide architecture direction together. - You will own operational health: data migrations, schema/platform updates, and triage of pipeline tickets, directly supporting the SDE team's work. - This is a high-visibility role: the data you deliver, and keep running, directly shapes what Alexa proactively tells customers, and when. Key job responsibilities 1. Partner closely with SDEs to help define data strategy, architecture direction, and the long-term roadmap for the team's data platform. 2. Design, build, and own ETL/ELT pipelines that ingest, transform, and load customer-interaction and context data at a scale of billions of records per day. 3. Own operational items end-to-end: data migrations, schema and platform updates, and triage/resolution of data-pipeline tickets, providing day-to-day support to the SDE team. 4. Partner with applied scientists and ML engineers to define data contracts, feature pipelines, and data-quality checks feeding personalization and proactive-agent models. 5. Operate and continuously improve production pipelines: optimize data delivery, redesign for scalability, manage deployments, and drive root-cause fixes for pipeline incidents. 6. Establish and document best practices for data modeling, warehousing, and pipeline design across the team. A day in the life You'll join SDEs in a design discussion to shape data strategy and architecture, then pick up a migration or platform-update ticket and see it through to resolution. You'll trace a data-quality issue in a personalization feature pipeline, support SDEs with any operational asks on your pipelines, and monitor the health of systems processing billions of daily customer-interaction events. You'll partner with applied scientists to onboard new signal sources and triage pipeline alerts. About the team Alexa AI - ML Engineering builds the personalization and proactive-intelligence systems that let Alexa anticipate what customers need before they ask. Data Engineers work side-by-side with SDEs and applied scientists, combining data strategy and large-scale engineering to turn billions of daily customer-interaction signals into the context, features, and content that drive Alexa's ranking, personalization, and proactive-agent experiences. We value ownership, data quality, and working backwards from the customer. - 3+ years of data engineering experience - 4+ years of SQL experience - Experience with data modeling, warehousing and building ETL pipelines - Experience with AWS technologies like Redshift, S3, AWS Glue, EMR, Kinesis, FireHose, Lambda, and IAM roles and permissions - Experience with non-relational databases / data stores (object storage, document or key-value stores, graph databases, column-family databases) Our inclusive culture empowers Amazonians to deliver the best results for our customers. jobs.title: Stage : Construction automatique de modèles de processus hospitaliers multi- flux par grands modèles de langage (LLM)
jobs.jd: Projet porté par : Marwa Trabelsi - IMT Mines Albi Centre Génie Industriel (CGI) Partenaires IMT impliqués : Telecom Sud Paris, Département Electronique et Physique, Laboratoire Services répartis, Architectures, Modélisation, Validation, Administration des Réseaux (SAMOVAR): Nel Samama Mines Saint-Etienne : Centre Ingénierie Santé (CIS), Marius Huguet Sujet proposé (5-6 mois à partir de Février): Acronyme : HOPAL : Hospital Process Automatic Learning Titre long : Construction automatique de modèles de processus hospitaliers multi-flux par grands modèles de langage (LLM) Description du projet : L’étude du processus de prise en charge aux urgences est essentielle pour comprendre et résoudre le problème croissant de surcharge, qui touche de nombreux pays. Cette surcharge, souvent liée à un déséquilibre entre la demande de soins et les ressources disponibles, a des conséquences graves : retards de traitement, allongement des temps de triage, et même une augmentation de la mortalité. Elle révèle aussi des défis systémiques, comme l’accès difficile aux soins primaires, qui poussent les patients vers les urgences. Optimiser l’utilisation des ressources humaines et matérielles permet non seulement de réduire les files d’attente, mais aussi d’améliorer la qualité des soins et l’efficacité globale du système. Enfin, analyser ces processus aide à identifier des solutions durables, comme une meilleure organisation ou une réallocation ciblée des moyens. Ces processus laissent des traces numériques dans le système d'information hospitalier (SIH), mais leur modélisation reste aujourd'hui largement manuelle, coûteuse et rapidement obsolète. Le process mining permet de découvrir des modèles de processus à partir de ces traces. Les techniques classiques de découverte atteignent toutefois leurs limites face à des logs hétérogènes, bruités et multi-flux. Les grands modèles de langage (LLM) ouvrent une voie nouvelle : générer automatiquement des modèles de processus (BPMN, graphes de processus) directement à partir de traces organisationnelles, sans intervention humaine, et en produire une lecture compréhensible par les acteurs de terrain. Par ailleurs, des travaux menés au CGI ont démontré la faisabilité de la prédiction de parcours patients par LLM. La question scientifique au cœur de ce stage est l'articulation de ces deux briques : comment relier la prédiction de parcours à la construction automatique de modèles, pour passer de modèles rétrospectifs (ce qui s'est passé) à des modèles prospectifs (ce qui va se passer) ? Ce projet s’inscrit dans une dynamique inter-écoles IMT autour de l’IA explicable pour la santé publique. Les équipes CGI, CIS et SAMOVAR collaborent déjà via le projet TRACKING (Carnot M.I.N.E.S – CARINGS), avec des travaux sur la géolocalisation indoor au sein des urgences de l’Hôpital Le Corbusier de Firminy. Cette synergie s’est prolongée par un stage M2 en 2025, financé par le Fonds d’amorçage Santé, dédié au prototypage d’une application mobile de localisation indoor/outdoor des patients. Une thèse INTERCARNOT a été lancé dans la continuité avec la validation des deux instituts Carnot (M.I.N.E.S et TSN) et va démarrer en Octobre 2026. Objectif du stage L'objectif est de concevoir et prototyper un pipeline dans lequel un même module de construction automatique de modèles par LLM est alimenté par deux sources : Branche A (rétrospective) : les logs SIH réels, normalisés en event logs, produisent des modèles as-is des processus observés ; Branche B (prospective) : dans la suite des travaux réalisés, les parcours prédits par LLM sont sérialisés au même format de traces (activité, timestamp, ressource) via un adaptateur, et produisent des modèles to-be des processus à venir. La comparaison des modèles as-is et to-be permet la détection d'écarts, l'anticipation des goulots d'étranglement et le support à la décision explicable, jusqu'à la simulation contrefactuelle (perturber les prédictions, reconstruire le modèle, observer l'impact). Profil recherché Formation : M2 ou dernière année d'école d'ingénieur en informatique, science des données, IA ou génie industriel ; Compétences techniques : Python indispensable ; une expérience des LLM (fine-tuning, prompting, API) et/ou du process mining (pm4py) est un atout fort ; Qualités : rigueur scientifique, autonomie, goût pour le travail avec des données réelles imparfaites, intérêt pour le domaine hospitalier. Références Huguet M, Pehlivan C, Ballereau F, Dodane-Loyenet A, Fontanili F, Garaix T, Yordanov Y, Augusto V, Tazarourte K, Redjaline A. jobs.title: Data Scientist - Machine Learning - RealAdvisor
jobs.jd: 🧭 About RealAdvisor RealAdvisor is one of the leading digital platforms in the European real estate ecosystem. Founded in Switzerland, we now support 7,000+ real estate agencies and attract 10+ million users per year across Europe. We are scaling fast across multiple markets with a clear mission: help real estate professionals grow through data, transparency and smart technology. At RealAdvisor, we value ownership, autonomy and impact. Role Overview We are looking for a business‑oriented Data Scientist to join RealAdvisor. You will consolidate and analyze diverse data sources (product, marketing, transactional), build ML models and experiments to drive subscription growth, and translate insights into concrete product and marketing actions. This is a hands‑on, full‑stack role: you will query databases, run experiments, build models, and present clear data stories to stakeholders. Requirements Key responsibilities Consolidate and aggregate data from product, marketing, CRM, and transactional systems into reliable datasets. Perform product analytics to measure feature usage, user journeys, and retention drivers. Design and run experiments (A/B tests, cohort analysis, population and variation control) to validate hypotheses and measure causal impact. Build ML models for revenue optimization, churn prediction, segmentation, and subscription forecasting. Analyze marketing performance to measure acquisition efficiency, LTV, and campaign ROI. jobs.title: Data Scientist, FX Quantitative Research
jobs.jd:
Who we are

About Stripe

Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies—from the world's largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups—use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone's reach while doing the most important work of your career.

About the team

Data Science at Stripe is a vibrant community where data scientists and data analysts learn and grow together. The Treasury Finance Data Science team builds the models, risk frameworks, and decision tools behind how Stripe manages money at global scale: liquidity, funding, counterparty risk, and foreign exchange.

Stripe moves funds across 135+ currencies every day. That creates FX exposure from merchant flows, multi-currency balances, and entity funding. In this role, you'll be a thought partner and builder alongside Stripe's FX team. Together you'll develop the quantitative foundation for how Stripe measures, forecasts, and hedges FX exposure.

What you'll do

You'll be the senior quantitative lead for FX within Treasury Finance Data Science. You'll co-build with Treasury, the FX hedging team, Finance, and Engineering: shaping the research agenda, turning ideas into rigorous models, and building the systems that put those models to work. Data Science owns these systems. They produce the decision-critical outputs and analyses that the FX team and Treasury leadership rely on. This is a hands-on role. You'll design the methodology, write the code, and ship it into production.

Responsibilities

  • Partner with the FX team to build and evolve FX risk measurement: exposure aggregation across entities and currencies, VaR / Expected Shortfall, stress testing, and scenario analysis
  • Develop forecasting models for FX exposures and multi-currency cash flows. Quantify forecast uncertainty so it can inform hedge sizing and timing.
  • Co-design hedge optimization and decision frameworks with the FX team that weigh hedge cost, residual risk, P&L volatility, and liquidity constraints
  • Build ML and statistical systems for trading and risk (signal research, anomaly detection on flows, execution and cost analytics), and take them from prototype to production
  • Own the production systems that generate decision-critical FX outputs, partnering with Engineering on reliability, SLAs, monitoring, alerting, and incident response for risk-critical workflows
  • Partner deeply with Treasury Finance stakeholders to turn business questions into quantitative frameworks. Anticipate needs and help shape FX risk strategy rather than reacting to requests.
  • Produce clear, trusted analyses and reporting that inform Treasury and Finance leadership decisions, including leadership-level reporting such as MBRs and QBRs
  • Use AI tools (code assistants, LLM-based agents) to speed up modeling, analysis, and automation, while maintaining rigor, validation, and auditability
  • Raise the technical bar for FX quantitative work within Data Science: methodology standards, model validation, documentation, and mentoring other data scientists

Who you are

We're looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements to be considered for the role. If you meet these requirements, you are encouraged to apply. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement.

Location Requirement

  • New York, NY required (50% in office - hybrid)

Minimum requirements

  • PhD with 1-3 years, MS or MA with 2-6 years, or BS or BA with 4-8 years of data science or quantitative modeling experience
  • Hands-on quantitative experience at a bank, asset manager, hedge fund, trading firm, or similar financial institution, with direct exposure to FX, rates, or market risk
  • Strong foundation in statistics, probability, and time-series modeling, plus working knowledge of risk measures (VaR, Expected Shortfall, stress testing) and hedging instruments (forwards, swaps, options)
  • Proficiency in Python and SQL. You write production-quality code, not just research scripts.
  • Experience taking models or analytical systems from research into production
  • Business acumen and the ability to turn complex analyses into clear, decision-ready insights
  • Ability to clearly communicate results and drive impact with cross-functional partners, including senior non-technical stakeholders
  • Ability to manage multiple projects at once, with strong attention to detail
  • Experience using AI tools to speed up modeling, analysis, and coding

Preferred qualifications

jobs.title: Applied ML Engineer/Data Scientist
jobs.jd: 🍇 About grape: Our entrepreneurial spirit drives us in what we do and what we are passionate about. Our mission is to become the premier health partner in the insurance business. Recognising the need for innovation in the traditional employee insurance model we are set to revolutionize the employee insurance industry. We help companies support people before and after they get sick and to make more of their time. Our insurance solutions reduce monotonous and manual work for employees, doctors, HR & payroll managers. As we strive to lead a technology-driven transformation, we put employees first. At grape we pride ourselves on our people and our culture. We continue to grow fast and that’s where you come in. Our team is dynamic, diverse and full of creative ideas. Want to join? We can’t wait to get to know you! Your role Our data and tech give us an edge in risk assessment, pricing and premium calculation. This role turns that into accurate models that support our carrier partners and our growth, builds tuned models where they beat rules and off-the-shelf LLMs in claims (triage, intervention, return-to-work, fraud), and responsibly explores how data can help employees stay healthy through grape Care. We’re looking for an applied ML engineer / data scientist to build predictive models from the ground up on real, regulated insurance data. You’ll own problems end to end, from effective-dated records to production, in a domain where correctness and responsible use genuinely matter. Starting points include pricing and risk, portfolio monitoring, claims and payment patterns, triage and return-to-work, absence, and fraud detection. grape sits on a rich dataset, though, and you’ll help find the next high-value use cases. You’re candid about what the data can support, and you propose simpler approaches when they’re the right answer. This is not an LLM role. LLM and agent workflows and document extraction sit with our engineering teams, and you’ll use their outputs as features. What you'll do: Build and validate models Own the full model lifecycle: feature engineering, training, evaluation, explainability, deployment, and drift monitoring. Backtest on the historical book and run models in shadow mode alongside human decision-makers, reporting where and why they disagree. Produce audit-ready validation and governance documentation that actuarial, compliance, and carrier partners can review. Platform and MLOps Deploy models on grape’s cloud platform within strict security and data-residency requirements for health data. Set up experiment tracking, model versioning, and production monitoring, partnering with engineering on integration. Shape the problem space Identify and prioritize high-value use cases as you explore the dataset, rather than waiting to be handed problems. Turn ambiguous business questions into well-defined, measurable modelling. Responsible & explainable by design Build privacy, fairness, and explainability into every model that touches personal or health data, working with compliance and legal on nDSG/GDPR boundaries. Models support decisions; accountable owners make them. Pricing, reserving, and claims work requires licensed-actuary sign-off, and any automation requires governance approval first. Collaborate Explain model behavior and limits to underwriting, claims, actuarial, and compliance teams. What you'll need: Strong applied ML and statistics: supervised and unsupervised learning, anomaly detection, time-series, and survival/duration modeling. Proven experience building models on real-world, relational, effective-dated data, including imbalanced outcomes. Fluent Python (pandas, scikit-learn, a modern ML stack) and strong SQL. Solid grasp of validation, calibration, and explainability (e.g. SHAP). Production MLOps: experiment tracking, versioning, and drift monitoring. Sound judgment on data privacy and modelling. Fluent English. Bias for action, ownership, and clear cross-functional communication. Big plus: Insurance, actuarial, or risk modeling (pricing, reserving, loss ratios). Health, disability, or absence data, especially Swiss insurance (KTG, UVG); fraud detection in claims. Regulated special-category data under nDSG/GDPR, or model risk management. Google Cloud, including security-restricted deployments. German language skills. 🤝 What we offer in return: 🌱 Empowering workplace: Join a passionate team and an empowering workplace where you are given the ownership, tools, and support to make decisions and take initiative. Together we grow and build innovative solutions. 💻 Hybrid setup: Enjoy the flexibility of our hybrid work schedule, with the freedom to work remotely or from our office in Zurich. On Thursdays, our team day, we meet together in our Zurich office. 🪑 Home office stipend: To enable our hybrid setup, we allocate a one-off CHF 200.- home office budget to help you set up your dream workspace in the comfort of your own home. 🌐 Internet allowance: We give you a monthly internet allowance to help cover your internet costs at home and enable you to work seamlessly from your home office. ⏳ Flexible working time: You can distribute your working hours the way you want to. 🧠 Learning budget: We support you in improving your skills, acquiring new knowledge and advancing your career. jobs.title: Senior Backend & AI Engineer (Remote)
jobs.jd: This role is open only to candidates living in the EU or EEA. We can't consider applications from other locations. If you've built something before, start here The hardest part of a startup usually isn't the code. It's finding customers who really need what you build and getting them to change how they work. At Scalera, that part is done: manufacturers, suppliers and contractors across Switzerland, Austria and Germany already run their tenders through us every day. What we need now are people who can take the next unsolved problem and turn it into a product customers can't do without. If you've founded a company (whether it worked out or not), been the first engineer somewhere, or built something people paid for, this role was written for you. About Scalera Scalera is an ETH Zurich spin-off building AI for the €200B+ European construction industry. Large manufacturers and suppliers still run their most document-heavy processes by hand, from reading 300-page tenders to retyping purchase orders into their ERP. We automate them one by one. Our product matching already handles 1,400 tender positions in 16 minutes at 98% precision, work that used to take a sales rep most of a day. What you'll do You'll be part product manager, part engineer. You'll spend real time with customers and help shape what we build. Sometimes you'll spot the next problem yourself, and sometimes we'll hand you a clear priority to run with. Spend real time with customers. Join calls and site visits, sit with the people who do the work, and understand why they do it the way they do. You'll know their problems firsthand, not from a ticket. Shape what to build. Turn what you hear into a clear problem, a scope and a plan, and push back when the obvious request isn't the real need. When we bring you a priority, you'll own how it gets solved. Build it. Design and build backend services in Go and Python that turn messy tenders, catalogs and purchase orders into data customers can rely on. Ship, then check. Get it in front of customers fast, watch how they actually use it, and iterate. Own it in production. When something breaks at a customer, it's yours to understand and fix. Build with AI. Use AI heavily in how you work, and design systems that agents can use as well as people. What success looks like after 3 months There's a part of the product people now think of as yours, and you're the one deciding what happens to it next You've spotted a problem nobody asked you to solve, made the case for it, and shipped a first version You've shipped features from both sources: priorities we set and ideas from your own customer conversations At least once, you've talked us out of building something customers didn't really need You've left a part of the platform simpler than you found it You'll probably thrive here if You've taken something from zero to one: a company, a product line, or a side project with paying users You've built and run backend systems in production that other people depend on. We care more about your judgment than your language; you're strong in Go or Python and happy to work in both You're solid on data modeling, API design and messy real-world data You'd rather talk to a customer than wait for a spec You're comfortable with ambiguity. You can make progress while the problem is still half-defined, which at a startup it usually is You want a large scope of responsibility and are happy to own things well beyond your job title Rapidly changing requirements don't throw you. When customers or priorities shift, you adapt and keep going You enjoy direct customer contact and want to be on customer calls You make things simpler over time, not more clever You write clearly in English. German is a plus, not a requirement You probably won't enjoy it if You just want to code and go home You don't like talking to customers, whether on calls or on the occasional site visit Ambiguity and chaos bother you You want a well-defined backlog handed to you Your main goal is managing people soon. Here, scope grows with what you own, not with headcount Our stack Go and Python (FastAPI), PostgreSQL, GCP, and LLMs throughout the document pipeline. You don't need to know all of it on day one. How we hire Screening call (30 min) with our VP Engineering. It's two-way: ask us anything, including the hard questions. Technical deep-dive call : walk us through something you built from scratch, the decisions you made and what went wrong. Meet Scalera Day : join us remotely to work on a real problem with real (anonymized) construction documents, and meet the team. Offer : if it's a fit on both sides, we'll move quickly to an offer. Working at Scalera Remote within the EU or EEA Small team, no bureaucracy. You'll work directly with the CEO, CTO, VP Engineering and Customer Success Competitive compensation Founders and former founders: if you're unsure whether you fit, send a few lines about what you built and why you moved on. We read every one. Find Jobs in Switzerland on Arbeitnow

jobs.title: Research Engineer, Benchmarks & Evaluation
jobs.jd: ABOUT RAMP Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $275B in annualized spend flows in and out of 85,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books. The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving. We hire people with high agency and high urgency. We look for slope over intercept. We care less about where you trained and more about what you’ve built. At Ramp, everyone is a builder who owns problems end to end and makes consequential decisions that shape the outcome. The median Ramp customer saves 7.5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year – far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same. If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it. ABOUT RAMP LABS Ramp Labs is Ramp's AI research group. We post-train models on finance work, build the environments and evals they learn from, and ship them into the products 70,000+ companies use to move money. We think the defensible part of an AI product is the loop: proprietary environments, evals that track what customers care about, and models trained against both. jobs.title: AI Research Engineer
jobs.jd: At Dscout , we’re building the most flexible and powerful UX research platform on the market—trusted by the world’s top brands in finance (JP Morgan Chase, Intuit, Charles Schwab, PayPal), healthcare (Aya, Headspace), consumer goods (Keen, Verizon, Target, Northface), and tech (Google, Amazon, Facebook, Meta, Spotify, AirBnB). Our tools help teams deeply understand the humans behind their products, so they can build better ones. We are expanding our smart and driven team and would love for you to join us. At Dscout, we're building the human-grounded layer that teaches AI to work in the real world and proves it stays aligned there. We are expanding our smart and driven team and would love for you to join us. Dscout AI Training & Evals builds human data and evals that show whether AI works for real people. For ten years Dscout has captured how people behave in real context, with consent and scientific rigor. Dscout AI Training & Evals points that engine at AI: consented human behavior and judgment, turned into the training data, evals, and benchmarks AI teams trust. Models ace benchmarks and still surprise people in the wild. A benchmark says how capable a model is. It does not say whether the model works for the person using it, across weeks, in the mess of real life. That gap is where we work. We serve AI researchers, the product builders who ship alongside them, and the research teams who partner with both. We are a new unit inside an established company: live customers, a mature platform (React, Elixir, Python, Swift, Kotlin; SOC 2 and HITRUST certified), a small senior team, and room to build. We work AI-native. Agents write code, evals gate changes, and we aim to do in months what used to take years. A note from our Chief AI Officer & GM. The hardest AI problems show up when a model meets real people, with their tools, their interruptions, and their goals. Our customers need a partner who can design the answer, build it, and ship it fast. Ground Truth sits where deployment meets research: what we learn in the field shapes the science, and the science shapes what we ship. Come build it with us. Why this seat Work on a problem the field has not solved: measuring whether AI works for real people, over real time. Study something most evals do not have: real participants, doing real tasks in their own context. Own the benchmark. You are founding it, not joining a team that has one. Publish. Methods and benchmarks go to the research community, with first authorship on the benchmark. Join a small senior team with direct access to the Head of AI Research and the GM. This is a research-first role focused on questions where the right rubric, benchmark, or method does not yet exist. You will find the gaps, propose bold directions, and take projects from the first hypothesis through experiments and benchmark construction to publication. You will also build: the science has to run inside live customer programs. What you will do Rubrics and QA science Design rubrics and test whether they measure what they claim: validity, reliability, and sensitivity. Measure how reliable human raters are, and when disagreement is noise versus real signal. Calibrate AI judges against real human judgment, and study when they drift away from it. Build quality signals that put evidence behind every data point we ship. Long-horizon, real-user benchmarks Design Dscout’s first benchmark: real users, in real context, over long horizons. Multi-week tasks across tools, not one-shot prompts. Define the protocol, task design, scoring, and release. Work with our delivery team on fieldwork. Work out how to keep a living benchmark honest over time: drift, contamination, difficulty, and what counts as a meaningful change. Write the paper and own the public release. Human judgment as training and eval signal Study when real-world human feedback improves a model and when it adds noise. Explore how preference and judgment data from representative people differ from expert data. Turn findings into methods our forward deployed engineers and delivery team can run in the field. New research directions These areas are the core, not the whole list. You will have significant latitude to propose new programs, such as calibrating user simulations against real behavior, human-AI collaboration, and behavioral evaluation of agents. Co-author with outside labs and academics on studies that need real-user data. Help run our paper-reading group. A good first year A QA and rubric framework running on live customer programs, with documented validity. Benchmark v0 released, with a paper submitted to a top venue. At least one external team using or citing our work. Delivery colleagues using your methods without needing you in the room. How we will hire: a conversation with the Head of AI Research; a research talk on your publication; a design exercise (how would you validate a rubric for a long-horizon task?); a conversation with the GM, forward deployed engineers, and delivery partners. What we care about most. A strong publication record helps. We care most about whether you can find the question that matters, design a rigorous way to answer it, and move fast enough that the answer is still useful. What you bring Published research in evals, preference learning, reward modeling, human-AI interaction, measurement, or agent evaluation. A PhD, a PhD in progress, or an MS with two or more strong research internships at labs or top industry groups. If you do not have advanced degrees but have a history of creative machine learning research work, this is just as desirable. Strong applied statistics: inter-rater reliability, confidence intervals, power, and a nose for when a metric misleads. Hands-on experience with LLM-as-judge, rubric-based evaluation, and preference data. Strong Python, and the ability to build research prototypes and evaluation pipelines other people run. You use AI coding tools as a real part of your workflow. Experience running expe

jobs.title: Senior AI/ML Engineer
jobs.jd: This role is also open to candidates living in the EU or EEA. We can't consider applications from other locations. If you've built something before, start here Most ML jobs hand you a benchmark. This one hands you a business problem with paying customers and their real data. Construction tenders are long, messy and full of trade jargon, and every decision a customer makes on our platform becomes a labeled example you can train on. We need someone who can turn that data into models that customers notice: from the first experiment to the model serving production traffic, and back again when a customer says it got something wrong. If you've founded a company (whether it worked out or not), been the first ML engineer somewhere, or shipped a model people paid for, this role was written for you. About Scalera Scalera is an ETH Zurich spin-off building AI for the €200B+ European construction industry. Manufacturers, wholesalers and suppliers in Switzerland, Austria and Germany still run their most document-heavy work by hand, from reading 300-page tenders to retyping purchase orders into their ERP. We automate that work one process at a time, and ML sits at the center of every one of them. What you'll own You'll own the ML behind our products, end to end. In practice that means: Training and fine-tuning : embedding models, rerankers, classifiers and LLMs, trained on our own data. Document understanding : models that pull structure, quantities and product specs out of tenders, orders and catalogs. Product matching : retrieval and LLM agents that match tender positions to the right products. Evaluation : offline benchmarks, per-customer evals and gates that keep a new model from shipping if it makes things worse. Training and serving infrastructure : automated retrain pipelines, GPU serving and vector search in production. Customer problems : when a model gets something wrong for a customer, finding out why and fixing it. What success looks like after 3 months There's a model or part of the pipeline people now think of as yours, and you're the one deciding what happens to it next. You've spotted a problem nobody asked you to solve, made the case for it, and shipped a first version. A model you trained runs in production, and customers can see the difference in their results. Retraining runs automatically, and nothing reaches customers without passing an eval you designed. You've cut LLM cost or latency by replacing an expensive step with a smaller model of your own. You've decided at least one thing we should stop building. You'll probably thrive here if You've taken something from zero to one: a company, a model in production, or a side project with real users. You've trained and fine-tuned models yourself, ideally embeddings, retrieval or document models, and evaluated them honestly on held-out data. You've built with LLMs in production and know where agents fail. You write strong Python and can run what you build: Docker, CI/CD, and cloud on GCP, AWS or Azure. You measure before you believe, and a single aggregate score doesn't convince you. You'd rather open a customer's actual document than wait for a spec. You're comfortable with ambiguity. You can make progress while the problem is still half-defined, which at a startup it usually is. You want a large scope of responsibility and are happy to own things well beyond your job title. Rapidly changing requirements don't throw you. When customers or priorities shift, you adapt and keep going. You enjoy direct customer contact and want to be on customer calls. You write clearly in English. German is a plus, not a requirement. You probably won't enjoy it if You just want to code and go home. You don't like talking to customers. Ambiguity and chaos bother you. You want a well-defined research agenda handed to you. You'd rather hand a model to someone else to deploy and debug. Your main goal is managing people soon. Here, scope grows with what you own, not with headcount. Our stack Python and PyTorch, open-weight and frontier LLMs, LangGraph, Langfuse, PostgreSQL with pgvector, Pinecone, and GCP. You don't need to know all of it on day one. How we hire Screening call (30 min) with our VP Engineering. It's two-way: ask us anything, including the hard questions. Technical deep-dive call : walk us through a model or system you built, the decisions you made and what went wrong in production. Meet Scalera Day : come to our office in Zürich, work on a real problem with real (anonymized) tender data, and meet the team. Offer : if it's a fit on both sides, we'll move quickly to an offer. Working at Scalera Zürich HQ, four days in the office, Fridays remote. If not located in Zürich then this role is open to remote within the EU or EEA, Occasional customer visits across Switzerland, Austria and Germany Small team, no bureaucracy. You'll work directly with the CEO, CTO, VP Engineering and Customer Success Competitive salary and meaningful equity Founders and former founders: if you're unsure whether you fit, send a few lines about what you built and why you moved on. We read every one. Find more English Speaking Jobs in Switzerland on Arbeitnow

jobs.title: Data Scientist, Analytics Enablement
jobs.jd: ABOUT THE TEAM The Strategic Finance Data Science team helps OpenAI understand business performance and make informed decisions about growth, revenue, and resource allocation. We partner with Strategic Finance, Data Engineering, and business teams to build trusted metrics, explain what is changing, and support forecasting, planning, pricing, and investment decisions. ABOUT THE ROLE We’re looking for a Data Scientist, Analytics Enablement to turn complex financial and business questions into reliable data products, clear analyses, and actionable recommendations. You will work across the analytical workflow: define the question, establish trustworthy metrics and datasets, investigate the drivers, and help partners act on the findings. This is a hands-on individual contributor role. You will combine the technical depth of analytics engineering with strong analytical judgment and close partnership with Strategic Finance. Your work will serve both executive reviews and the teams making day-to-day business decisions. IN THIS ROLE, YOU WILL - Define and maintain trusted metrics and analytical datasets for revenue, usage, customer performance, compute consumption, and margin, with clear definitions and appropriate product, customer, and cohort detail. - Build automated dashboards and recurring reporting that help Finance leaders and operating teams understand performance, spot changes, and prioritize investigation. - Explain movements in business results and variances against expectations by examining underlying drivers, validating data quality, and distinguishing evidence from assumptions. - Translate ambiguous questions about growth, retention, monetization, pricing, and resource efficiency into structured analyses and practical recommendations. - Partner with forecasting specialists and Finance to provide reliable inputs, driver analyses, and scenario assumptions for forecasts and long-range plans. - Work with Data Engineering to improve the quality and usability of underlying data, and develop reusable analytical models and workflows that reduce manual effort. - Communicate findings clearly, align stakeholders on trade-offs, and follow through to understand whether the analysis or data product improved the decision. YOU MIGHT THRIVE IN THIS ROLE IF YOU - Have strong SQL and analytical data-modeling skills, and experience turning large, complex datasets into reliable analyses and reusable data products. - Can reason carefully about metrics, cohorts, denominators, measurement changes, and uncertainty, and investigate whether an unexpected result reflects the business or the data. - Have built dashboards or recurring reporting used by business partners, and can explain the decisions they enabled. - Bring sound business judgment and can independently scope an ambiguous problem, prioritize the work, and deliver an end-to-end solution. - Communicate technical findings clearly and work effectively with Finance, data scientists, engineers, and other business partners. - Can use Python or a comparable analytical tool to investigate data and automate repetitive work. jobs.title: Data Scientist, FX Quantitative Research
jobs.jd:
Who we are

About Stripe

Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies—from the world's largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups—use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone's reach while doing the most important work of your career.

About the team

Data Science at Stripe is a vibrant community where data scientists and data analysts learn and grow together. The Treasury Finance Data Science team builds the models, risk frameworks, and decision tools behind how Stripe manages money at global scale: liquidity, funding, counterparty risk, and foreign exchange.

Stripe moves funds across 135+ currencies every day. That creates FX exposure from merchant flows, multi-currency balances, and entity funding. In this role, you'll be a thought partner and builder alongside Stripe's FX team. Together you'll develop the quantitative foundation for how Stripe measures, forecasts, and hedges FX exposure.

What you'll do

You'll be the senior quantitative lead for FX within Treasury Finance Data Science. You'll co-build with Treasury, the FX hedging team, Finance, and Engineering: shaping the research agenda, turning ideas into rigorous models, and building the systems that put those models to work. Data Science owns these systems. They produce the decision-critical outputs and analyses that the FX team and Treasury leadership rely on. This is a hands-on role. You'll design the methodology, write the code, and ship it into production.

Responsibilities

  • Partner with the FX team to build and evolve FX risk measurement: exposure aggregation across entities and currencies, VaR / Expected Shortfall, stress testing, and scenario analysis
  • Develop forecasting models for FX exposures and multi-currency cash flows. Quantify forecast uncertainty so it can inform hedge sizing and timing.
  • Co-design hedge optimization and decision frameworks with the FX team that weigh hedge cost, residual risk, P&L volatility, and liquidity constraints
  • Build ML and statistical systems for trading and risk (signal research, anomaly detection on flows, execution and cost analytics), and take them from prototype to production
  • Own the production systems that generate decision-critical FX outputs, partnering with Engineering on reliability, SLAs, monitoring, alerting, and incident response for risk-critical workflows
  • Partner deeply with Treasury Finance stakeholders to turn business questions into quantitative frameworks. Anticipate needs and help shape FX risk strategy rather than reacting to requests.
  • Produce clear, trusted analyses and reporting that inform Treasury and Finance leadership decisions, including leadership-level reporting such as MBRs and QBRs
  • Use AI tools (code assistants, LLM-based agents) to speed up modeling, analysis, and automation, while maintaining rigor, validation, and auditability
  • Raise the technical bar for FX quantitative work within Data Science: methodology standards, model validation, documentation, and mentoring other data scientists

Who you are

We're looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements to be considered for the role. If you meet these requirements, you are encouraged to apply. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement.

Minimum requirements

  • BS/BA with 8+ years, MS/MA with 6+ years, or PhD with 3+ years of full-time experience in quantitative finance, risk modeling, quantitative research, or data science
  • Hands-on quantitative experience at a bank, asset manager, hedge fund, trading firm, or similar financial institution, with direct exposure to FX, rates, or market risk
  • Strong foundation in statistics, probability, and time-series modeling, plus working knowledge of risk measures (VaR, Expected Shortfall, stress testing) and hedging instruments (forwards, swaps, options)
  • Proficiency in Python and SQL. You write production-quality code, not just research scripts.
  • Experience taking models or analytical systems from research into production
  • Business acumen and the ability to turn complex analyses into clear, decision-ready insights
  • Ability to clearly communicate results and drive impact with cross-functional partners, including senior non-technical stakeholders
  • Ability to manage multiple projects at once, with strong attention to detail
  • Experience using AI tools to speed up modeling, analysis, and coding

Preferred qualifications

  • MS or PhD in a quantitative field (e.g., Quantitative / Mathematical Finance, Financial Engineering, Statistics, Mathematics, Physics, Computer Science, Economics, Operations Research)
  • Applied machine learning experience in trading or risk (e.g., forecasting, execution analytics, signal research, anomaly detection)
  • Experience with corporate treasury or balance-sheet FX: multi-entity exposure management, hedge programs, and treasury concepts such as liquidity, funding, and cash positioning
  • Experience building risk or decision systems with engineering standards: code review, testing, monitoring, and defined SLAs
  • Experience with distributed data tools (e.g., Spark) and workflow orchestration (e.g., Airflow, Flyte)
  • Prior experience at a growth-stage internet, fintech, or payments company
  • Experience creating leadership-level reporting, such as QBRs and MBRs
  • A builder's mindset, with a willingness to question assumptions and conventional wisdom
  • Interest in how data products enable automated a

jobs.jd: NVIDIA has helped redefine what computers can do. Now, generative AI is opening new possibilities for how people learn, create, and tackle problems. Realizing that potential means answering some of the hardest questions in AI: Where do models fall short? Which risks are we missing? How do we know our safeguards are working? As an expert in machine learning for Evaluations, you’ll help establish the evidence that guides the next generation of safer AI. Your curiosity and scientific judgment can shape what we test, what we learn, and what we build next. We are looking for a Machine Learning Engineer / AI Researcher / Data Scientist to join our AI Safety and Responsibility efforts within Enterprise Risk Management. Engaging directly in engineering tasks, you will apply your data science and statistics skills. You will turn open research questions into rigorous benchmarks, inventive experiments, and tools that reveal how multimodal large language models behave under pressure. Working with researchers and platform engineers, you’ll connect those discoveries to better training methods and safeguards, with reproducible results that inform technical reviews and executive decisions. If you love asking the question no one has thought to test, and building a convincing way to answer it, come help us define what progress in AI safety looks like. What You Will Be Doing: Safety Benchmarking: Design and maintain safety benchmarks for large language and multimodal models, translating risk scenarios into test cases, datasets, and scoring rubrics. Evaluation Methodology: Define metrics and protocols that assess safety alongside model usefulness, using baselines, uncertainty estimates, and failure analysis to distinguish meaningful improvements from noise. Reproducible Evaluation: Build reusable Python pipelines with versioned datasets, model configurations, and experiment tracking to reproduce results and compare performance across model releases. Automated Red-Teaming: Develop tools to discover failure modes and expand evaluation coverage, incorporating human review to validate automated scoring and provide additional judgment. Failure Analysis: Investigate model failures with researchers, document actionable findings, and develop regression tests to assess whether model changes resolve identified issues. Results and Communication: Partner with platform engineers to store and aggregate evaluation results, and clearly communicate findings, limitations, and emerging risks to researchers and decision-makers. What We Need To See: Education and Experience: Bachelor’s degree or equivalent experience, with 6+ years in the field of machine learning engineering or evaluation. Evaluation Design: Experience developing benchmarks, metrics, and statistically sound comparisons for ML systems, including selecting baselines and interpreting uncertainty. Ability to translate ambiguous evaluation questions into testable experiments. Engineering: Strong Python skills and experience building maintainable shared tools, data pipelines, and experiment-tracking workflows. Analytical Rigor: Ability to assess dataset quality, identify limitations in metrics and scoring methods, and support conclusions with reproducible evidence. Communication: Clearly explain findings and tradeoffs to researchers, engineering partners, and executives. Ways to Stand Out from the Crowd: Evaluation: Experience evaluating LLMs, multimodal models, or agentic systems through adversarial testing or automated red-teaming. Community Contributions: Contributions to public benchmarks or evaluation frameworks. Research Publications: A publication track record and interest in continuing to publish at top tier venues. Human-Aligned Evaluation: Experience validating model-based evaluators against human judgments or designing human-in-the-loop evaluation workflows. Statistical Rigor: Strong model evaluation skills and a commitment to sound statistical practices, including confidence intervals. jobs.jd: The Role We're building the runtime infrastructure that powers Moveworks' AI agents — the systems that orchestrate, execute, and deliver agent responses to millions of enterprise users in real time. This role sits where large language models meet distributed systems. You'll apply machine learning, LLM, and distributed systems expertise to make agents plan, reason, and use tools reliably, and you'll build the production systems that run those agents at enterprise scale. Our AI agents can plan, execute multi-step workflows, call tools, wait on human input, and resume — all while maintaining correctness, observability, and low latency. The systems that make this possible are what you'll build and own. What you get to do in this role: Agent orchestration engine — A state machine that manages long-running agent sessions, coordinating planning, execution, and user interaction across multiple LLM calls and tool invocations Model routing and adaptation — Choose, route between, and fine-tune or distill LLMs for specific agent tasks. Meet enterprise requirements such as granular permissions, data freshness, explainability, and preserving general knowledge. Distributed session management — Lease-based ownership using conditional writes, heartbeat protocols, and crash recovery via checkpointing Event-driven message pipeline — FIFO queues for ordered delivery, consumers for event processing, and real-time streaming via gRPC and Socket.IO Structured concurrency — Running multiple concurrent tasks per session with fail-fast semantics and graceful cancellation Observability infrastructure — OpenTelemetry instrumentation, distributed trace context propagation across async boundaries, custom span lifecycle management for sessions that span minutes Caching and state layers — Redis, DynamoDB KV stores with per-org/per-bot scoping, batch read optimization, and hot-reload configuration Tool and agent connectivity for LLMs: Build MCP and agent-to-agent (A2A) capabilities, including tool discovery, namespacing, and tool selection over large tool catalogs, so the LLM picks and calls the right tool from thousands of candidates. Token efficiency and context engineering — Lower the agent's cost and latency through prompt and context discipline, caching, speculative and parallel model-call scheduling, and reducing tokens spent across multi-step LLM reasoning chains. Open-weights model adoption and evaluation — Quickly stand up newly released open-weights LLMs at different quantization levels, run them in a test environment, and benchmark their accuracy, latency and cost on agent tasks. Use the results to decide which models reach production. To be successful in this role you have: You should have deep experience in at least 3 of these areas: Distributed systems: consistency models, idempotency, exactly-once delivery, distributed locking/leasing Concurrent/async programming: Python asyncio, Go goroutines, structured concurrency, cancellation handling Event-driven architectures: message queues (SQS, Kafka), pub/sub, backpressure, delivery guarantees Database systems for infrastructure: DynamoDB (conditional writes, transactions), Redis (connection pooling, pub/sub) Observability: OpenTelemetry, distributed tracing, span context propagation, Prometheus metrics gRPC/protobuf: streaming RPCs, service interface design, error handling patterns Machine learning: Large language models, natural language processing, LLM evaluation Required: 5+ years building production backend/infrastructure systems Strong in Python or Go (ideally both) Experience designing and operating systems that handle real traffic at scale Hands-on experience building production systems that use LLMs or other ML models Comfort with ambiguity — these are novel problems without textbook solutions Relevant past experience: Building and shipping products on large language models with techniques such as RAG, chain-of-thought, self-reflection, tool and function calling, and agentic reasoning. Training, fine-tuning, or evaluating machine learning models on large datasets in production, especially for NLP, retrieval, or ranking. jobs.jd: About the Singapore AI Center of Excellence (COE) The Singapore AI Center of Excellence (COE) is a dedicated engineering and R&D hub focused on Enterprise and Sovereign AI. Our mission is to help organizations move AI workflows cleanly into production through two main paths: creating reusable software architectures that solve common industry problems, and contributing code directly to upstream open-source projects to fix enterprise gaps in system deployment, runtime tuning, and platform management. Basing our engineering team in Singapore creates a close feedback loop between customers, partners, and core product teams. This direct connection keeps our development roadmaps relevant, speeds up solution delivery, and strengthens our ability to co-innovate across the region. Role Overview The AI/ML Engineer is a highly technical, hands-on role at the intersection of Enterprise AI and client-facing architecture. As part of our Customer Engineering function, you will write production-grade solution blueprints alongside strategic customers and technology partners. Your mission is to solve immediate, high-stakes operational bottlenecks in the APAC region by delivering repeatable, extensible, and open-sourced AI Quickstarts that show the industry how to solve complex challenges. In this team, career growth and seniority are defined purely by your technical competence, architectural depth, and ability to deliver end-to-end solutions autonomously in highly ambiguous environments. There is no expectation of team management, project coordination, or formal talent mentorship; your progression is driven entirely by engineering impact. What You Will Do: Enterprise-Minded Blueprinting: Design and build comprehensive, production-ready architecture blueprints and reference codebases. These blueprints must naturally take into account critical enterprise requirements—including systems-level hardening, infrastructure scalability, and network isolation boundaries—without you needing to perform the last-mile hands-on production deployment yourself. Open-Source AI Quickstarts: Package repeatable, extensible technical architectures as open-sourced AI Quickstarts to solve complex, real-world industry problems and accelerate ecosystem adoption. Co-Development & Integration: Collaborate with external engineering teams (such as semiconductor partners, regional AI programs, and software vendors) to validate joint-architecture blueprints, ensuring stable integrations across the system stack. Benchmarking & Evaluation: Design and integrate automated testing, evaluation harnesses, and system-level telemetry into blueprints to monitor and measure performance metrics like latency, throughput, cost, and model quality. Regulated & Secure Design: Proactively incorporate robust data privacy standards, secure network perimeters, and localized hosting considerations into all solution blueprints to satisfy compliance and risk management requirements in highly regulated environments. What You Will Bring: Academic & Professional Experience Education: Bachelor’s or Master's degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, or a related quantitative field. Software Engineering Foundations: Excellent understanding of software engineering fundamentals, including clean code principles, test-driven development (TDD), CI/CD automation pipelines, and version control (Git) workflows. Communication: Clear verbal and written communication skills in English, with the ability to articulate complex technical architectures to other engineers and technical stakeholders. Core Technical Stack Programming Languages: Exceptional, hands-on proficiency in Python (specifically for machine learning and systems programming). Solid familiarity with lower-level system languages such as Go or C/C++ is highly preferred. Deep Learning & ML Libraries: Strong familiarity with PyTorch and core NLP/vision ecosystems (e.g., Hugging Face Transformers, datasets, and tokenizers). Cloud-Native Frameworks: Strong practical experience deploying containerized applications on Kubernetes or production-grade enterprise container orchestration platforms. Base MLOps Knowledge: Conceptual and hands-on understanding of model serving lifecycles, data ingestion steps, and automated packaging. Target Knowledge Domains & Growth Areas We are building a multi-disciplinary engineering squad. Candidates are expected to bring experience in some of the following domains, and will have the opportunity to continuously develop their skills across all of them as they grow in seniority: Platform & Pipeline Engineering: Experience with distributed computing frameworks and cluster schedulers (such as Ray), workflow orchestration (such as MLflow or Kubeflow), distributed unstructured data parsing tools (such as Docling), and vector database structures. Generative AI & Agentic Architectures: Familiarity with LLM orchestration engines (such as LangChain, LlamaIndex, or LangGraph), agentic workflows (AgentOps), tool-calling protocols (such as Model Context Protocol) and model fine-tuning (PEFT/SFT). Hardware Heterogeneity & Runtime Optimization: Understanding of model serving runtimes (such as vLLM), optimizing engines for latency and throughput (e.g., KV cache offloading, chunked prefill), and running benchmarks across diverse hardware setups including CUDA, ROCm, and emerging GPU/NPU architectures. Regulated Deployments: Designing isolated, air-gapped container networks, secure registry services, and local inference environments to meet strict data residency, privacy, and compliance policies. Nice-to-Have: Industry Domain Experience While not strictly required, experience applying AI/ML architectures to solve challenges in the following regulated industries is a strong advantage: Financial Services (FSI): Familiarity with risk-assessment models, fraud detection patterns, or compliance requirements under regulatory frameworks. jobs.jd: Reddit is a community of communities. It’s built on shared interests, passion, and trust, and is home to the most open and authentic conversations on the internet. Every day, Reddit users submit, vote, and comment on the topics they care most about. With 100,000+ active communities and approximately 130 million daily active unique visitors, Reddit is one of the internet’s largest sources of information. For more information, visit www.redditinc.com . At Reddit, machine learning sits at the heart of how millions of people discover, connect, and engage with the world’s largest collection of human conversations. From “How do I fix a leaky faucet?” to “What should I watch next?”, the Answers Relevance team leverages AI to connect people with the real-world wisdom of Reddit communities. We’re hiring Senior and Staff Machine Learning Engineers to make Answers smarter, more relevant, and more helpful. Our SOTA AI systems helps surface the right conversations, but the heart of Answers is still people helping people ~ Redditors sharing what they know with each other! What You’ll Work On You’ll lead ML projects from idea to production, partnering with Product, Data Science, and Engineering across recommendations, search, messaging, and AI systems. jobs.title: Forward Deployed Engineer
jobs.location: USA, CA, Pleasanton USA, GA, Atlanta
jobs.jd: Your work days are brighter here. We’re obsessed with making hard work pay off, for our people, our customers, and the world around us. As a Fortune 500 company and a leading AI platform for managing people, money, and agents, we’re shaping the future of work so teams can reach their potential and focus on what matters most. The minute you join, you’ll feel it. Not just in the products we build, but in how we show up for each other. Our culture is rooted in integrity, empathy, and shared enthusiasm. We’re in this together, tackling big challenges with bold ideas and genuine care. We look for curious minds and courageous collaborators who bring sun-drenched optimism and drive. Whether you're building smarter solutions, supporting customers, or creating a space where everyone belongs, you’ll do meaningful work with Workmates who’ve got your back. In return, we’ll give you the trust to take risks, the tools to grow, the skills to develop and the support of a company invested in you for the long haul. So, if you want to inspire a brighter work day for everyone, including yourself, you’ve found a match in Workday, and we hope to be a match for you too. About the Team The Forward Deployed Engineering (FDE) organization sits at the intersection of Product, Engineering, and customer execution across Agent Factory, Sana, Data Cloud, and the Developer Platform. When Workday launches new AI agents and platform capabilities, early deployments surface complex real-world challenges, from unstructured tenant data and intricate configurations to edge-case enterprise workflows. The Developer Platform FDE team focuses on agent development: custom AI agents and agentic apps that run on Workday rails and surface anywhere. We work with the customers building their own agents on the Workday Developer Platform, using the same infrastructure Workday uses to power its own agents. Every agent we help ship inherits the security model, business process controls, and audit trail of the system of record for people and money at some of the world’s largest organizations, and thanks to open protocols, those agents can show up in Workday, in Sana, or inside the AI tools people already use every day. FDEs also serve as a critical feedback engine for Product and Engineering. On the Developer Platform team, you’ll build production agents with Developer Agent, Agent-Ready Tools, and the Agent Harness, and work directly with the product and engineering teams behind those tools. Field insights, recurring customer friction, and proven build patterns become scalable, out-of-the-box capabilities that reach every developer building on Workday. It’s a team where deep technical skill meets real customer impact every day, with direct influence over where the platform goes next. About the Role As a Forward Deployed Engineer on the Developer Platform FDE team, you’ll combine hands-on agent engineering with direct customer work. Working alongside senior FDEs, you’ll help enterprise customers build, deploy, and optimize custom AI agents and agentic apps inside live customer environments. You’ll work with the full Workday Developer Platform stack. You’ll run custom agents on the Workday Agent Harness, the same agent runtime and infrastructure Workday uses internally. You’ll build agents, apps, and orchestrations in plain language with Developer Agent, from the Workday Developer Site, a VS Code–compatible IDE plug-in, or any other MCP-compatible agentic tool, such as Claude Code, Cursor, or Codex. You’ll wire agents into hundreds of governed, LLM-native Agent-Ready Tools for HR and finance data over MCP, and build with industry-leading ADKs and agent frameworks. You’ll connect agents to each other and to the places people work using open standards like MCP, A2A, and A2UI, alongside REST APIs. And you’ll do it with governance built in, not bolted on, through Workday Extend AI, the Agent System of Record, Agent Passport, and Workday Data Cloud. You’ll work across the full deployment lifecycle alongside senior FDEs, AI Deployment Architects, Product Managers, and Workday Services leads. You’ll help drive immediate customer success while building deep expertise in enterprise agent engineering, and every engagement will sharpen both your technical skills and your sense of what makes a platform great to build on. What you'll do: Agent Engineering & Deployment: Build, configure, test, and debug custom AI agents and agentic apps inside live enterprise tenants, working against live data, business processes, and security configurations. Customer Discovery & Solution Support: Participate in technical discovery sessions with customer stakeholders, and help translate business requirements into product configurations, POCs, and integration specs. Developer Toolkit Feedback: Be a hands-on, everyday user of Developer Agent, Agent-Ready Tools, and the Agent Harness. Document bugs, edge-case failures, and friction points with clear reproduction steps and context, and share them with Developer, AI, and Integration Platform product teams to improve the developer toolkit for the open Workday ecosystem. Productization of Field Insights: Spot recurring deployment challenges and contribute fixes, reusable components, sample code, and documentation to the reference architectures, playbooks, and pattern guidance that let customers and partners build without us. Building Total Agentic Systems with Fellow FDEs: Work with FDEs across Workday’s other agent areas, including first-party agents, Sana, Data Cloud, and Deployment AI, to deliver complete agentic systems. For example, you might help pair a custom agent built on the Developer Platform with Workday’s first-party agents, orchestrate them through Sana over A2A, and ground them in Data Cloud. Engagement Milestones & Delivery: Own defined technical workstreams within customer engagements and help guide them through structured milestones, from kickoff to graduation, within standard 6-month deployment cycles.
